open_blockers.finding: Completed replay accepts marker-only synthetic fault logs, does not rerun exact wrapper/safety validation, and does not preserve or bind the four post-fault recovery controls.

The delegated wildcard publication can bless an arbitrary caller tree without root fixed-scorer replay or reservation/output binding. Rename/chown/chmod does not revoke a caller's pre-open writable file descriptor, and completed replay does not reconstruct the canonical result from capture evidence.
After publication, the unprivileged controller attempts to reopen the result under a root-only mode-0700 parent and must fail after the irreversible transition.

evidence: publish_p1_result validates only caller-manifest equality and approval candidate before issuing a root receipt.
The passing root publication fixture contains only arbitrary attempt.json and summary.json.
The installer creates p1-results root:root mode 0700, while the controller reopens the returned child path.
Linux retains write authority on a pre-open O_RDWR file description across rename, chown and chmod.

candidate_14_scope: Root independently copies every source artifact into newly created root-owned files, semantically runs the fixed completed-result validator on that copy, and only then issues a receipt.
Publication is bound to the permanent reservation, exact output identity, approved commit and installed controller hash; direct/repeated/forged publication fails.
Completed evidence preserves and revalidates full fault and post-fault control logs, exact wrapper/safety markers, token/logit fingerprints, and capture-to-canonical lineage.
The unprivileged controller exact-compares the root receipt and does not traverse root-only storage.
